newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Foreign direct investment in S.Korea soars 65 pct.
newsitem.headline: Foreign direct investment in S.Korea soars 65 pct.

text.p: Foreign investment in South Korea, excluding portfolio investment, rose 64.9 percent to $3.20 billion in 1996 from $1.94 billion in 1995, the finance ministry said on Monday.

A ministry statement said foreign investment in the manufacturing sector totalled $1.93 billion in 1996, up from $884 million in 1995. Non-manufacturing investment increased to $1.27 billion from $1.06 billion.
A ministry official said South Korea's deregulation and expanded tax incentives contributed to the rise.

By country, the United States was the largest investor in South Korea with $877 million last year, up from $645 million in 1995. Japan followed with $253 million, down from $418 million, while investment from the European Union rose to $892 million from $461 million.
